title: Uniform small-prime arithmetic first-jet regularity density with Arakelov lifting
difficulty_reason: The old uniform inverse-p-square upper bound for smooth irreducible fibers does not recover the Euler-factor density with an error uniform in degree and small prime, nor cover singular fibers. The authors separately control the singular part of a bad fiber using rank-n differential data rather than the rank-(n-1) smooth locus, then absorb the finitely many exceptional fibers. They coordinate the prime-dependent power N(p) with the maximal jet-surjectivity cutoff r_(p,d), prove its admissibility under C n p^n<d, and combine the medium/high-degree and Euler-tail estimates into O((d/p)^(-2/n)) uniformly in d,p. These additional quantitative and singular-fiber obligations remain after the old derivative-decoupling, evaluation and lifting framework is allowed; Theorem4.1's Arakelov transfer belongs to the same unit.

editorial_notes: Regular projective arithmetic variety of absolute dimension n, integral/flat/projective over SpecZ in the original sense; ample Hermitian line bundle retains its three source positivity/generation conditions.
Strictly effective means sup norm<1, and Arakelov density is the degree-limit ratio for that fixed Hermitian bundle. Preserve exact source finite-dimensional section spaces.

The new4.1/4.2 statements require the printed C n p^n<d range and original large-degree quantifiers; their error constants are independent of d,p with fixed geometric/line-bundle data. Do not extend to arbitrary p or infinite uniformity.

The new fiber-density statement does not require smooth/irreducible X_p. Old2097Prop6.1 does. Retain the separate bad-fiber proof and finite-exception absorption rather than inserting a smoothness condition.
P'_(d,p^2) is the arithmetic first-order tangent condition dim(m/m²)=n-1. Do not replace it by smoothness of the reduced finite-field divisor or regularity of the thickened scheme itself.

Theorem1.1 concerns residual characteristics only up to exp(epsilon d); Theorem1.2 is only an upper-density bound for fully regular divisors. Cor1.3 is metric rescaling, not a further independent core.

AppendixA.1 states a finite-field density limit for ample L and smooth X inside a smooth open U of projective Y. The exponential bound O(d^m q^(-c d/p)) belongs to high-degree PropositionA.9, not the entire density convergence.

Keep original N0,N1,N(p), characteristic p, q and all coprimality/range/constant dependencies and author shorthand/unexpanded boundaries; no repaired formulas, added assumptions or independent correctness certification.

Complete original supporting4.3-4.13 and AppendixA inputs remain in the full work, including the non-smooth-fiber proof1402-1451 and uniform coordinate/exceptional-prime controls. Do not count mixed-characteristic full-jet or second lifting-coordinate mechanisms already covered by old2097 as new difficulty. Primary4.2 and lifted4.1 are one count, not two.
